### What happened?

https://github.com/RobotLocomotion/drake-external-examples/actions/runs/40325564370

As part of the `drake_poetry` CI in drake-external-examples, we set `PYTHONWARNINGS=error` before calling `poetry run python particle_test.py`. Poetry itself calls a deprecated API, and the corresponding warning is promoted to an error since the environment variable is set before running poetry.

To see this more clearly, the following should produce the same error:

```shell
export PYTHONWARNINGS=error
poetry --version
```

### Is there an already existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Expected behavior

The /dev/shm/fast_datasharing_* segment is, by construction, memory shared between the
writer process and one or more reader processes (the documentation explicitly recommends
co-mounting the same directory for cross-container data sharing). Shared, concurrently
writable state should be treated as input: indices and offsets read from it should be
validated against the extents that were actually allocated (history length, segment size,
payload max size) before being used in pointer arithmetic.
Expected: a segment whose descriptor, history array, or node metadata contains values
outside the allocated extents (written by a crashed peer mid-update, an external writer of
the file, or any corruption) is rejected or safely ignored, with a log line; the owner
process does not perform out-of-segment dereferences based on those values.

### Current behavior

Every structure read from the segment is trusted as-is. Writer side, on the payload
release path:

    src/cpp/rtps/DataSharing/WriterPool.hpp:318-334, WriterPool::advance_till_first_non_removed():

        auto offset = history_[static_cast<uint32_t>(descriptor_->notified_begin)];
        auto payload = static_cast<PayloadNode*>(segment_->get_address_from_offset(offset));
        if (!payload->has_been_removed()) ...

- the index into `history_` comes from the in-segment descriptor, unclamped;
- the offset read from `history_` is converted with raw boost-interprocess handle
  arithmetic and dereferenced, with no check that it falls inside the segment;
- when the removed-flag byte read through that pointer is 1, the loop then writes 0
  through the same pointer (has_been_removed(false)) and pushes the pointer into
  `free_payloads_`, so the next get_payload() hands it out as the destination of the next
  payload write (PayloadNode::reset() plus the serialized sample).

The ring arithmetic trusts the in-segment size as well: DataSharingPayloadPool::advance()
(DataSharingPayloadPool.cpp:42-54) computes the next index against
descriptor_->history_size, so a corrupted history_size lets the index walk past the array.

Reader side symmetric: ReaderPool::get_next_unread_payload (ReaderPool.hpp:204-205)
converts history_[next_payload_] the same way, and read_from_shared_history
(ReaderPool.hpp:238-265) takes the in-segment data_length verbatim as both length and
max_size.

Observed: writing two values into the live segment from another process of the same user
(history[0] = an offset outside the segment; descriptor notified_begin = 0,
notified_end = 1) makes the writer SEGV on its next history eviction, within one write
cycle; the stack trace is attached in the "Relevant log output" section. A control run
with the segment untouched completes cleanly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a DataSharing-eligible pair on master: a bounded, non-keyed topic type
   (TopicDataType::is_bounded() == true, plain), DataWriter with PREALLOCATED memory mode,
   BEST_EFFORT reliability, KEEP_LAST depth 1, default DATA_SHARING (AUTO). The writer
   writes a small sample every 200 ms; the segment
   /dev/shm/fast_datasharing_<prefix>_0.0.1.3 appears once the writer is created.

2. From another process of the same user, open the segment read-write with
   boost::interprocess (managed_shared_memory open_only), locate the two named chunks
   ("descriptor" as PoolDescriptor, "history" as Offset[]), and set:
       history[0] = 0xFFFFFFF0        // an offset far outside the segment
       descriptor->notified_begin = 0
       descriptor->notified_end   = 1

3. Wait for the writer's next write (<= 200 ms). The KEEP_LAST(1) eviction calls
   release_payload -> advance_till_first_non_removed, which converts history[0] and
   dereferences it: SEGV.

Control: identical pair, no modification of the segment: the writer completes its whole
run and exits normally.

### Fast DDS version/commit

master @ 51521ef (upstream, 2026-10-20)

### Platform/Architecture

Other. Please specify in Additional context section.

### Transport layer

UDPv4

### Additional context

Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 22.04), ASan build. Discovery runs over UDPv4; the crash path is the
DataSharing payload pool in the POSIX shared-memory segment, not a network transport.
Preconditions to observe this behavior, stated plainly: the segment file must be writable
by whatever modifies it. With the default 0644 permissions on /dev/shm/fast_datasharing_*,
that means another process of the same user on the same machine, or root. There is no
network path to this state, and no cross-user path: other users can read the segment
(that is a separate permission question) but not write it. Separate containers do not see
each other's /dev/shm at all under default isolation; they only share segments when
explicitly configured to (--ipc=host, --ipc=container:<x>, Kubernetes hostIPC, or a
co-mounted directory configured as the data-sharing directory), and even then the
permission bits still require both sides to run the same uid.
To be explicit about scope: the set of scenarios that can trigger this is narrow. It
requires write access to the segment, which in practice means a process already running
as the same user or root on the same machine (or the explicitly-shared container setups
above). No remote, cross-user, or default-cross-container reachability is claimed. The
reason it is still worth a report is limited to the failure mode itself: the corruption
turns into out-of-segment pointer arithmetic inside the owner process instead of a
rejected, logged condition.


### XML configuration file

```xml

```

### Relevant log output

```shell
# AddressSanitizer runtime report on stderr (the reproducer is an ASan build);
# the ==41063== prefix is the pid of the crashing writer process.
==41063==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x7f8b6a5ffff1
==41063==The signal is caused by a READ memory access.
    #0 ... WriterPool::advance_till_first_non_removed() .../rtps/DataSharing/WriterPool.hpp:324
    #1 ... WriterPool::release_payload(SerializedPayload_t&) .../rtps/DataSharing/WriterPool.hpp:121
    #2 ... WriterHistory::release_change(CacheChange_t*) .../rtps/history/WriterHistory.cpp:454
    #3 ... WriterHistory::remove_change_nts(...) .../rtps/history/WriterHistory.cpp:291
    #4 ... History::remove_change(...) .../rtps/history/History.cpp:145
    #5 ... DataWriterHistory::remove_change_pub(...) .../fastdds/publisher/DataWriterHistory.cpp:400
    ...
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV .../WriterPool.hpp:324 in WriterPool::advance_till_first_non_removed()
```

### Network traffic capture

_No response_

new_candidates.body:
### Is there an already existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Expected behavior

With `-DSECURITY=ON`, the security artifact providers should pick their OpenSSL includes from the OpenSSL version actually installed. On OpenSSL 3.x and 4.x that is the `openssl/types.h` branch, and the build should not depend on `openssl/engine.h` (the ENGINE API is deprecated since 3.0 and OpenSSL builds configured with `no-engine` do not install that header).

### Current behavior

`src/cpp/security/artifact_providers/Pkcs11Provider.hpp` and `src/cpp/security/artifact_providers/FileProvider.hpp` test the OpenSSL version before any OpenSSL header has been included:

```cpp
#include <string>

#if OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x30000000L
#include <openssl/engine.h>
#include <openssl/err.h>
#include <openssl/ssl.h>
#else
#include <openssl/types.h>
#endif // if OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER < 0x30000000L
```

At that point `OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER` is not defined, so the preprocessor evaluates it as `0` and the pre-3.0 branch is always taken, whatever OpenSSL is installed. The build only works on OpenSSL 3.x today because most distributions still ship `openssl/engine.h`.

On a distribution whose OpenSSL is configured with `no-engine` (Fedora 44, OpenSSL 3.5.9) that header does not exist and every translation unit that reaches these headers fails:

```
In file included from .../src/cpp/security/authentication/PKIDH.h:24,
                 from .../src/cpp/rtps/security/SecurityPluginFactory.cpp:20:
.../src/cpp/security/artifact_providers/Pkcs11Provider.hpp:25:10: fatal error: openssl/engine.h: No such file or directory
   25 | #include <openssl/engine.h>
      |          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
compilation terminated.
```

The same pattern is still present on `master` (51521ef, 2026-10-20).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fedora 44 (`openssl-devel-3.5.9-1.fc44`, which has no `/usr/include/openssl/engine.h`).
2. `cmake -DSECURITY=ON ..` on Fast DDS 3.6.2 (or master) and build.
3. `SecurityPluginFactory.cpp`, `PKIDH.cpp` and the other security TUs that include `PKIDH.h` fail as above.

Fix: include `<openssl/opensslv.h>` before the version test in both headers. With that one include the test becomes meaningful: OpenSSL 3.x and 4.x take the `openssl/types.h` branch, OpenSSL 1.1 still takes the `engine.h` branch, and the build succeeds on Fedora 44 with all security plugins compiled (verified: the resulting `libfastdds.so` loads `DDS:Auth:PKI-DH`, `DDS:Access:Permissions` and `DDS:Crypto:AES-GCM-GMAC` and a secured ROS 2 participant works). The patch is here: https://github.com/nickschuetz/ros2-rpm/blob/main/specs/lyrical/patches/fastdds/0003-opensslv-before-version-check.patch

Happy to open a PR with it against `master` if that is welcome.

### Fast DDS version/commit

3.6.2 (ROS 2 Lyrical `release/lyrical/fastdds/3.6.2-1`), also present on `master` at 51521ef94b85.

### Platform/Architecture

Other. Fedora 44 x86_64 and aarch64 (GCC 15, OpenSSL 3.5.9 configured with `no-engine`). Not a Tier 1 platform; filed as an issue rather than a discussion because it is a plain include-order bug that affects any OpenSSL build without the ENGINE headers.

### Transport layer

Default configuration, UDPv4 & SHM (not transport-related; build-time failure)

### Additional context

ROS 2 Lyrical, Fast DDS packaged as RPMs for Fedora. Related but separate: #6432 / #6487 (OpenSSL 4.0 `const X509_NAME*`), which this report does not cover.
new_candidates.title: Security build: OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER is tested before any OpenSSL include, so openssl/engine.h is always required

### Describe the bug

`Articulation.write_joint_friction_coefficient_to_sim_index` of the PhysX backend is annotated to accept `torch.Tensor | wp.array | float` for `joint_friction_coeff`, `joint_dynamic_friction_coeff` and `joint_viscous_friction_coeff`, as `BaseArticulation` declares, but any `float` fails with a Warp launch error. The method passes the values unchanged to the `write_joint_friction_data_to_buffer` kernel, whose inputs are 2-D arrays. Unlike the stiffness, damping, velocity limit, effort limit and armature writers, it has no scalar branch. The deprecated `write_joint_friction_coefficient_to_sim` and the `_mask` writer forward to it and fail the same way. The Newton and OVPhysX writers of the same name accept a `float`.

### Steps to reproduce

The Cartpole from `isaaclab_assets` on the default PhysX backend. Save the script as `repro.py` and run `python repro.py` (headless by default; add `--device cpu` for the CPU pipeline):

```python
import argparse

from isaaclab.app import add_launcher_args, launch_simulation
from isaaclab.utils import clone

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
add_launcher_args(parser)
args_cli = parser.parse_args()

import torch

import isaaclab.sim as sim_utils
from isaaclab.assets import Articulation
from isaaclab.sim import SimulationContext

from isaaclab_assets import CARTPOLE_CFG  # isort:skip

sim_cfg = sim_utils.SimulationCfg(device=args_cli.device)
with launch_simulation(sim_cfg, args_cli):
    sim = SimulationContext(sim_cfg)
    cfg = clone(CARTPOLE_CFG)
    cfg.prim_path = "/World/Robot"
    robot = Articulation(cfg)
    sim.reset()
    print(type(robot))
    robot.write_joint_armature_to_sim_index(armature=0.01)  # a scalar works here
    friction = torch.full_like(robot.data.joint_friction_coeff.torch, 0.5)
    robot.write_joint_friction_coefficient_to_sim_index(joint_friction_coeff=friction)  # a tensor works
    robot.write_joint_friction_coefficient_to_sim_index(joint_friction_coeff=0.25)  # a scalar fails
    print("joint_friction_coeff:", robot.data.joint_friction_coeff.torch)
```

```
<class 'isaaclab_physx.assets.articulation.articulation.Articulation'>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../source/isaaclab_physx/isaaclab_physx/assets/articulation/articulation.py", line 2109, in write_joint_friction_coefficient_to_sim_index
    wp.launch(
  File ".../warp/_src/context.py", line 11333, in launch
    pack_args(fwd_args, params, adjoint=False)
  File ".../warp/_src/context.py", line 11328, in pack_args
    params.append(pack_arg(kernel, arg_type, arg_name, a, device, adjoint))
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../warp/_src/context.py", line 10327, in pack_arg
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: Error launching kernel 'write_joint_friction_data_to_buffer', argument 'in_friction' expects an array of type array(ndim=2, dtype=float32), but passed value has type float.
```

A `float` for `joint_dynamic_friction_coeff` or `joint_viscous_friction_coeff` fails the same way (`argument 'in_dynamic_friction'` or `'in_viscous_friction'`), with `--device cuda:0` and `--device cpu`.

### System Info

- Commit: main 727e4e43ab; the same code is in v3.0.0 (e3f7d9ff1f) and release/3.0.0 (961760bcb9)
- Isaac Sim Version: 6.2.0.0 (pip)
- Warp 1.17.0, PyTorch 2.11.0 (cu130)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- GPU: RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell
- CUDA: 13.0
- GPU Driver: 580.126.20

### Additional context

In 2.3 the writer documented "Scalars are broadcast to all selections." and assigned the values with torch indexing (`self._data.joint_friction_coeff[env_ids, joint_ids] = joint_friction_coeff`).

### Checklist

- [x] I have checked that there is no similar issue in the repo (**required**)
- [x] I have checked that the issue is not in running Isaac Sim itself and is related to the repo

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On PhysX, a `float` for any of the three friction coefficients writes the same values as an equal tensor, and `None` for the dynamic or viscous coefficient still leaves it unchanged.
